title: Map, Set, WeakMap, and WeakSet
summary: Choose a collection based on whether you need unique values or key lookup.
nestedConcepts: Associate data with objects using WeakMap

subtopics.title: Store key-value pairs with Map
subtopics.explanation: A `Map` stores values under keys and keeps the order in which keys were added. Unlike a plain object, a key can be any value, including an object. Use `get`, `set`, `has`, and `delete` when the collection is keyed by data rather than fixed property names.

subtopics.title: Keep unique values with Set
subtopics.explanation: A `Set` stores each value once and preserves insertion order. Adding a value already present does not create a duplicate. For example, use `new Set(tags)` to remove repeated tags, then use `has(tag)` for a direct membership check.

subtopics.title: Associate data with objects using WeakMap
subtopics.explanation: A `WeakMap` uses objects as keys and does not keep a key object alive solely because it appears in the map. This suits private metadata tied to an object’s lifetime. WeakMaps cannot be iterated, so use a regular `Map` when you need to list or count every entry.

subtopics.title: Track object membership with WeakSet
subtopics.explanation: A `WeakSet` tracks whether an object is a member without making that object stay in memory just because of the set. It is useful for marking objects that have been processed. It only accepts objects and cannot be enumerated; use `Set` when values must be listed.

subtopics.title: Choose the right collection
subtopics.explanation: Use an array when position, repeated values, or mapping over every item matters. Use a `Set` for unique membership checks, and a `Map` when each key identifies a value. Choose weak collections only when object lifetime and non-enumerability are useful parts of the design.

foundations.overview: A Map stores key and value pairs and accepts many key types. A Set stores unique values. WeakMap and WeakSet hold object references weakly, so they do not keep otherwise-unused objects alive. Weak collections cannot be looped over.
foundations.mentalModel: A Set is a guest list with no duplicates; a Map is a labeled set of lockers.
foundations.whyItMatters: The right collection makes relationships clearer and avoids awkward array searches.

keyTakeaways: WeakMap keys must be objects and are weakly held.
WeakSet tracks object membership without keeping objects alive.
Use arrays when order and repeated values are the main need.
